{{Short description|Prize awarded by the Italian Mathematical Union}}
The '''Caccioppoli Prize''' is awarded by the [[Italian Mathematical Union]] to an Italian mathematician not exceeding the age of 38 who established a wide international reputation.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://umi.dm.unibo.it/caccioppoli/index-en.html |title=Caccioppoli Prize from the site of the Italian Mathematical Union |access-date=2011-12-17 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190514091912/http://umi.dm.unibo.it/caccioppoli/index-en.html |archive-date=2019-05-14 |url-status=dead }}</ref> The prize is entitled to the memory of the Italian mathematician [[Renato Caccioppoli]] and is awarded on the occasion of the Italian Mathematical Union conference every four years. In its early stages the prize was awarded every two years. The recipient currently receives 10,000 euros.

Further prizes of the Italian Mathematical Union are the [[Bartolozzi Prize]], the [[Stampacchia Medal]] and the [[Vinti Prize]].

== Prize winners ==
Source: [http://umi.dm.unibo.it/en/prizes/renato-caccioppoli-prize/ Unione Matematica Italiana]
Winners and relative academic affiliations at the time of the awarding of the prize
*1960 [[Ennio De Giorgi]] ([[Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa]])
*1962 [[Edoardo Vesentini]] ([[University of Pisa]])
*1964 [[Emilio Gagliardo]] ([[Università degli Studi di Genova|University of Genova]])
*1966 [[Enrico Bombieri]] ([[University of Pisa]])
*1968 [[Mario Miranda (mathematician)|Mario Miranda]] ([[University of Pisa]])
*1970 [[Claudio Baiocchi]] ([[University of Pavia]])
*1974 [[Alberto Tognoli]] ([[University of Pisa]])
*1978 [[Enrico Giusti]] ([[University of Pisa]])
*1982 [[Antonio Ambrosetti]] ([[International School for Advanced Studies]])
*1986 [[Corrado De Concini]] ([[Sapienza University of Rome|La Sapienza University of Rome]])
*1990 [[Gianni Dal Maso]] ([[International School for Advanced Studies]])
*1994 [[Nicola Fusco]] ([[University of Naples Federico II|University of Naples]])
*1998 [[Luigi Ambrosio]] ([[Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa]])
*2002 [[Giovanni_Alberti_(mathematician)|Giovanni Alberti]] ([[University of Pisa]])
*2006 [[Andrea Malchiodi]] ([[International School for Advanced Studies]])
*2010 [[Giuseppe Mingione]] ([[University of Parma]])
*2014 [[Camillo_De_Lellis_(mathematician)|Camillo De Lellis]] ([[University of Zürich]])
*2018 [[Valentino Tosatti]] ([[Northwestern University]])
*2022 [[Guido De Philippis]] ([[Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences]])
